apps.title: Every app, one list
apps.body: Each app you run is a project, and every project writes into the same inbox — colour-coded, filterable, one unread count. You are not signing in and out of four helpdesks.

noTickets.title: No support email, no ticket numbers
noTickets.body: Your users are already signed in to your app. Your server signs a short token and they are identified — no new account to make, no “please include your order ID”.

context.title: You can see what they were looking at
context.body: The chat attaches the page, record or item they were on when they wrote. It is sitting on the conversation before you have asked a single question.

connect.title: Connecting it is a ten-minute job.
connect.intro: Three steps. Your users never make an account, because they already have one with you — your server vouches for them with a token that lasts an hour.

step1.title: Create a project
step1.a: One project per app. You get a public key
step1.b: that’s safe in a browser and a secret
step1.c: that never leaves your server. Set the name replies are signed with, the origins allowed to host the chat, and who gets emailed when someone writes.

step2.title: Sign a token for the user who's signed in
step2.body: One authenticated route on your server. Any JWT library works; here it is with none at all.

step3.title: Drop the chat on the page
step3.body: A script tag and the function that fetches that token. That's the install.
step3.a: Only the origins you listed can host it — anywhere else sees an error and never gets a token. Add
step3.b: with a target element and the same chat becomes a page of your app instead of a floating bubble.

tour.title: Six tools’ worth of work, in one panel.

inbox.title: Every app, one conversation list.
inbox.body: Reply as the team, leave notes the customer never sees, and see who they are and what broke for them without leaving the thread.
inbox.b1: Colour-coded projects, one unread count, live updates
inbox.b2: Assign, prioritise, label and close, with custom fields per ticket type
inbox.b3: Their recent errors and linked planning items sit beside the chat
inbox.b4: Replies also go out by email when they are away
inbox.alt: The HelpBites inbox: a conversation list, a thread with an internal note, and the customer panel.

errors.title: Errors, with the fix attached.
errors.body: Connect GlitchTip or Bugsink and browse every issue with its stack trace, breadcrumbs and tags. Errors stay out of the inbox.
errors.b1: AI reads the stack trace and your GitHub repos, then suggests a fix
errors.b2: Or copy the same context as a prompt for your coding agent
errors.b3: Alert rules by email or Telegram: new error, total events, or N in a window
errors.alt: An error expanded to its stack trace, with a Fix with AI panel underneath.

board.title: Users say what to build. You decide what ships.
board.body: A public feedback page per project, and a private planning board behind it. Votes from linked posts add up on each card.
board.b1: Votes, comments, reactions and {'@'}mentions, with duplicates merged
board.b2: Link cards to feedback posts and inbox conversations
board.b3: Publish only the items you pick as a public roadmap
board.b4: Moving a card updates its linked posts, and emails their followers
board.alt: Planning: backlog, planned, in progress and done columns with vote counts on each card.

changelog.title: A changelog that writes its first draft.
changelog.body: Entries are drafted by AI from your GitHub commits or finished work, and wait for your review. Nothing is public until you approve it. When one ships, the people who asked for it hear about it.
changelog.b2: A public page, JSON and RSS, plus digest emails for readers
changelog.b3: Or write entries yourself, or from the command line
changelog.alt: The changelog panel with two AI drafts awaiting review and a published release.

email.title: Design once. Brand it per project.
email.body: A block designer that renders for Gmail, Apple Mail and Outlook, with an AI that turns pasted HTML into editable blocks.
email.b1: One shared template linked into every project, each with its own brand
email.b2: Checks for missing alt text, low contrast and placeholder links
email.b3: Send from your server with one API call, scheduled or per recipient
email.b4: Reusable components, share links, test sends, import and export
email.alt: The email designer with a layer tree, a newsletter preview and theme settings.

delivery.title: See every email that left, and what happened to it.
delivery.body: One entry per recipient, kept current by Mailgun. Bounces, complaints and unsubscribes are suppressed so you stop sending to them.
delivery.b1: Opened, clicked, bounced and skipped, filterable by template or source
delivery.b2: Contacts, segments, broadcasts and drip sequences with double opt-in
delivery.b3: Unsubscribe links and one-click headers by default
delivery.alt: The email delivery log with delivery statistics and per-recipient status.

flags.title: Switch a feature without a deploy.
flags.body: Off, on, or on for admins only, with an allow list. Your app reads them over the API, with a fallback for when we are unreachable.
flags.b1: Tag flags for frontend, backend or iOS
flags.b2: Your server reads the lot; a browser reads its own evaluated values
flags.alt: Two feature flags with Off, Admins only and On switches.

more.title: Small things that sit next to support.

stripe.title: Revenue from every place you sell
stripe.body: Connect Stripe, RevenueCat, the App Store, Paddle or Lemon Squeezy, or send payments from your own code, to see revenue, MRR and each person’s payments next to their conversations.

legal.title: Legal documents
legal.body: Draft a privacy policy, terms, cookie and refund policy from reviewed clauses, then host them on a public page. A starting point for your lawyer, not legal advice.

ai.title: Bring your own AI
ai.body: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, Mistral, Groq, xAI, DeepSeek or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Off until you switch it on.

telegram.title: Telegram alerts
telegram.body: Send a project’s error alerts to a Telegram chat as well as email. HelpBites only sends.

kb.title: Knowledge base
kb.body: Upload an FAQ and let an assistant answer from it, with routing rules that hand the rest to a person.

apple.title: iPhone, iPad and Mac
apple.body: A native app for the inbox, the email editor and most of the panel, with push notifications.

human.title: A person reads it, and a person answers.
human.body: AI is off until you switch it on for an assistant, and when it is on it answers only from the knowledge you gave it. No bot in the way by default, no “did that answer your question?”, no deflection funnel measured in tickets avoided. For most products, a chat window with a human on the other end is the entire feature.

run.title: It’s yours to run.
run.b: brings up the app, Mongo, Parse and Redis. Attachments go to any S3-compatible bucket you point it at. Your users’ conversations stay on infrastructure you control. Nothing phones home; the only outside services are the ones you connect, such as Mailgun or an LLM.
run.p2: The widget is a convenience, not the product. Everything it does is on the API, and the API is documented down to the response shapes — build your own chat UI on it if you’d rather.

app.title: In your app
app.hint: One script tag, no dependencies, about 10 KB.

bubble.term: A bubble, or a page of your app
bubble.desc: Give it a container and data-mode="inline" and the same chat becomes a page in your layout.

context.term: Knows what they were looking at
context.desc: Attach the page, record or link they are on, and update it as they move around your app.

onboarding.desc: Write welcome screens in the panel and show them once with one script tag or a SwiftUI file, in your users' languages. Your app keeps a copy, so they still show when HelpBites is unreachable.

pricing.desc: Plan cards, a paywall or a comparison table on your site and in your SwiftUI app. Prices and checkout come from Stripe; the names, features and buttons are yours, in your users’ languages and currencies. A/B test them and see which one sells more.

media.desc: Paste or pick PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP. Reply, unsend and react, and see when the team has read it.

colours.desc: Your Brand kit sets the accent, logo, typefaces and corner radius once. The chat, boards, forms, legal and blog pages and campaign mail all wear them.

none.desc: Every endpoint is public and documented. Build your own chat UI on /v1/* instead.

hub.desc: helpbites.js adds the chat, feedback board, changelog and onboarding your project has. A page at /hub gathers your changelog, roadmap, feedback, blog and legal documents, and the chat can open on a Home tab with what is new.

domains.desc: Put the feedback board, changelog or blog on feedback.yourapp.com. Add a TXT and a CNAME, and the page, the embeds and the API answer there with their own certificate.

inbox.title: In your inbox
inbox.hint: One panel, however many apps and teammates.

live.desc: Colour-coded projects, one unread count, and messages that arrive as they happen. Filter by assignee, status or unread.

overview.desc: The panel opens on an overview: a card per app with its unread and open conversations and revenue, one list of what needs attention (drafts to approve, failed syncs, bounces, fired alerts), the latest unread messages, and revenue by app. Each app has a setup checklist that turns green only when things really connect.

notes.desc: Internal notes your customer never sees. Their recent errors and linked planning items sit beside the conversation.

away.desc: Notify whoever you list per project. Replies go to users by email too, linking straight back to the thread.

first.desc: Start a conversation with a user, after a failed payment or before a migration.

native.desc: A native app for the inbox, replies and most of the panel, with push notifications once your server has APNs set up.

hub.desc: Their plan and MRR from Stripe, their earlier conversations and the feedback they asked for, which they follow. Reply from saved replies and FAQs, or have AI draft an answer from your knowledge for you to edit.

email.term: Mail to support@you becomes a conversation
email.desc: Give a project an address like support@yourapp.com, on your own domain or forwarded from your mailbox. Messages land in the inbox as conversations, and replies go back by email, threaded in your customer's mail app.

feedback.title: Feedback, roadmap, changelog and blog
feedback.hint: Users tell you what to build. You tell them what shipped.

board.desc: Users post ideas and bugs, vote, comment and react. You set the types, tags and statuses, and merge duplicates.

roadmap.term: A roadmap from your own planning
roadmap.desc: Plan internal work on a kanban, link it to posts and conversations, and publish only the items you pick. File an error on it in one click, and see the GitHub commits and pull requests that finished each item.

changelog.desc: Entries grouped into releases, drafted from finished work and reviewed before they go public. Includes RSS and digest emails.

blog.desc: Write posts and pages in a rich editor and publish them on a hosted blog in your own design, in your own site or by RSS, and email them to your subscribers. An AI writing helper drafts or improves posts from your GitHub repos. Members-only posts, SEO fields, a sitemap and an import from Ghost. Readers react and comment.

followers.desc: Email when a followed post changes status, gets a public reply, or mentions them. Anyone can mute or unfollow.

knowledge.title: Knowledge and AI assistants
knowledge.hint: Off until you turn it on. Grounded in your docs when it is on.

faq.desc: A Markdown or text file becomes a searchable knowledge base. Duplicates are flagged, and re-imports never overwrite your edits.

assistants.desc: Each one has its own instructions, your choice of OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and others (or any compatible endpoint), and routing rules that send a conversation to AI or to a person. Test a question first and see why it answers or hands over.

scope.desc: Assign knowledge per assistant, by area or by single FAQ, with exclusions. Test retrieval before it answers anyone.

hybrid.desc: Keyword and vector search over the knowledge base. It runs keyword-only if you skip embeddings.

email.title: Email and marketing
email.hint: Design once, brand per project, send from your server, see every delivery.

designer.desc: Sections, buttons, columns and reusable components, rendered for Gmail, Apple Mail and Outlook. An AI designer turns pasted HTML into blocks.

api.desc: POST a template, your own HTML or a block document, with per-recipient variables and language, attachments, scheduling and idempotency keys.

log.desc: One entry per recipient, kept current by Mailgun. Bounces, complaints and unsubscribes are suppressed automatically.

contacts.desc: Sync people from Postgres, Parse or Firestore, segment them, then run broadcasts and drip sequences with double opt-in.

forms.desc: Collect people before you launch with a single email box or a form of your own, with file uploads and in your visitors' language, on your site, a hosted page or in your app. Every sign-up becomes a contact with its own segment, double opt-in, a welcome email and a drip sequence.

team.title: Your team and your tools
team.hint: Roles, error tracking and flags that sit next to support.

errors.desc: Connect GlitchTip or Bugsink. Browse errors with their stack traces, get alert emails or Telegram messages when one spikes, file one on your board, and fix them with AI that reads your GitHub repos, on demand or as a scheduled report.

legal.desc: Draft a privacy policy, terms, cookie and refund policy from reviewed clauses, translate them with AI, then publish them on a page you link to.

brand.desc: Logos, app icons, screenshots, colours, fonts and guidelines on a public press page in one of three templates, with downloads and an embed for your site.

pages.term: Landing pages and a headless CMS
pages.desc: Build pages from templates and components in a visual editor, with animations, and host them. Or read the same content from your Vue, JavaScript or Swift app. An assistant writes the copy and new components, reading your GitHub repos.

flags.desc: Switch features on, off or for admins only, from the panel, without a deploy.

types.desc: Support is built in. Add types with their own statuses, fields and actions, and actions call back to your app over a signed webhook.

roles.desc: Agents answer, admins run projects and the team, owners handle billing. Invite people by email. Export a workspace or one project, or move it between self-hosted and cloud in one click.

mcp.term: Drive it from Claude or ChatGPT
mcp.desc: Connect any MCP assistant with one address. It reads the inbox, replies, triages feedback and writes changelog entries as you, with your role. Revoke it with one click.
